Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are David Patel, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Network Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Harper, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

David Patel: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments.

Our key achievements include significant progress in our fiber buildout, where we've accelerated homes passed and subscriber adoption amid competition from cable operators and satellite providers. The launch of our 5G Ultra Home fixed wireless access service is exceeding expectations, resulting in explosive subscriber growth and hundreds of millions in incremental revenue. Further milestones are our enterprise and B2B wins, including major private 5G contracts pushing segment revenue higher with robust margins. We are also focusing on ARPU expansion through targeted pricing and bundling, delivering solid year-over-year gains. Our dedication to optimizing revenue mix across wireless, broadband, media, and enterprise segments is bearing fruit, with favorable shifts to higher-margin areas. Our strategy is to manage cost of revenue trends effectively while investing in network and content. We are actively investing in EBITDA margin expansion through operational leverage. We are also exploring spectrum utilization enhancements and finally, analyzing new product impacts on overall growth.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $15.2 billion, reflecting a 6% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.2%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $2.5 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Good morning again, team. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our cost of revenue, which came in at $7.9 billion for the quarter, up 8% year-over-year from $7.3 billion in Q3 2023, but flat sequentially from Q2 2024's $7.9 billion. As a percentage of revenue, this represents 52% of our top line, expanding 200 basis points YoY due to targeted investments in our 5G Standalone core and premium content slate, partially offset by efficiency gains from our network virtualization program.

Network operations remain our largest bucket at $4.75 billion, or 60% of total cost of revenue, up 10% YoY. This includes site leases, backhaul transport, energy for base stations, and depreciation on our capex-heavy 5G assets. Content acquisition costs were $1.98 billion, or 25%, up 12% YoY amid fierce bidding for live sports rights. The balance—$1.23 billion, or 15%—covers customer premise equipment like 5G CPE routers and ONTs for fiber broadband, plus interconnect fees with peers.

Key trends and YoY drivers: Network costs at $4.75 billion rose 10% YoY, driven by accelerated 5G mid-band rollout with over 15,000 new C-band sites deployed since last year. This drove $660 million in incremental depreciation from tower collocations and small-cell densification. Energy costs spiked 15% or $225 million due to higher power draw from Massive MIMO radios with 25% higher utilization from 4K streaming and IoT traffic. Positively, Open RAN trials with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony shaved 5% off transport costs sequentially, saving $75 million through disaggregated architectures.

Content costs at $1.98 billion increased 12% YoY, with live sports rights jumping 18% to $850 million from NBA and Premier League renewals averaging $375 million annually. Offset by $150 million in savings from ad-supported tiers, where we've grown FAST channels 30% YoY to 280, leveraging free ad inventory to reduce linear carriage fees.

Other costs at $1.23 billion rose 2% YoY, with CPE flat at $565 million from volume discounts on modems. Interconnect fees up $38 million from peering with hyperscalers, mitigated by edge caching with Akamai.

Sequentially flat QoQ, but with a 3% uptick in variable network opex from summer data surges—mobile traffic up 22% YoY to 28 EB. Regionally, North America at 75% or $5.9 billion up 9% YoY from fiber overbuilds and CBRS amortization; Europe 15% or $1.2 billion up 5% moderated by green mandates; Asia-Pacific/LatAm 10% or $790 million up 15% from greenfields.

We're architecting for margin expansion via Network 2.0 with AI predictive maintenance targeting 10-15% opex reductions by FY2025, delivering $280 million in Q2 run-rate savings. On content, pivoting to originals reduces third-party reliance by 20% over two years.

For Q3, cost of revenue guides to $8.1-$8.3 billion, 3-5% QoQ growth but gross margins expanding 100 bps to 49%. Full-year on track for 7-9% growth below 12% revenue growth, driving levered FCF to $15 billion.

Next, our revenue mix underscores portfolio resilience. Total revenues $15.2 billion up 6% YoY. Wireless Services largest at 48% or $7.3 billion, up 6.8% from postpaid adds and ARPU to $55.42, with 5G SA at 85% coverage. Broadband/Wireline 22% or $3.3 billion flat YoY but service up 3.1%, FBB at 18 million subs. Media/Entertainment 18% or $2.7 billion up 12.4% from streaming adds. Enterprise/Wholesale 10% or $1.5 billion up 2.7% from private 5G. Other 2% or $320 million down 8%.

Mix shifted favorably YTD: Wireless to 48%, Media to 18%. Allocating 60% of $10 billion FY capex to 5G-Advanced and fiber for 10% service growth.

Blended postpaid ARPU $58.42, up 4.1% YoY from $56.14. Mobile $52.75 up 3.2% from 3-5% pricing hikes and 5G bundles adding $0.85 and $0.42. Broadband $67.20 up 6.8% from multi-gig premiums and Stream bundles at $1.80 attach. Video $46.30 down 1.2% offset by quadruple-play. US up 5.3%, LatAm +1.8%, APAC +7.2%. Q4 4-5% growth from pricing and AI upsell.

Adjusted EBITDA $5.8 billion at 38.2% margin, up 110 bps YoY. Q4 guide 39-40% or $5.9-$6.1 billion on $15.4-$15.6 billion revenue. FY2025 40.5-42% or $25.2-$26.1 billion on 5-7% revenue growth.

Tailwinds: Open RAN at 45% footprint saves 15-20% energy; wireless premiumization churn 0.71%; FWA to 2 million subs; Peacock-like streaming ARPU $8.20. North America 41-42%, Europe 35%. Headwinds capex 16-17%, content up 5% offset by ad tech. FCF 45% conversion for buybacks.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Lisa. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture.

I'd like to dive into our fiber-to-the-home buildout, a core growth driver. In Q3, we passed an additional 280,000 homes, bringing total fiber homes passed to 2.1 million—a 58% YoY increase on track for 2.8 million FY guidance. Sequential acceleration from Q2's 250,000, with footprint at 17% of 12-million-home SAM, density >80 homes/mile.

Deployed 14,000 strand miles, cumulative 55,000 since 2022. New DMAs like Raleigh-Durham 85,000 HHP via Duke Energy partnerships; Southeast 95% complete. Northeast 35% HHP with RDOF; Southeast 45% with XGS-PON on 40%; Midwest/West 20% MDU focus.

Over 65% XGS-PON capable for 10G symmetric, Wi-Fi 6E mesh cuts truck rolls 25%. Capex/home $825, down 12% QoQ for 3-4 year ROI.

Fiber subs 520,000 up 30% QoQ, 25% take rate up 300 bps, YTD 140,000 adds, churn 0.75%. Mature markets 38% pen, ARPU $148/month from gigabit/5G bundles, 70% 1G+.

Converted 18,000 cable cord-cutters. Moat-building with $500 million BEAD applications. Q4 300,000 HHP, 40,000 adds, 28% take. Outpacing peers.

We control 550 MHz average depth, 48,000 MHz-Pops. 25% low-band, 55% mid-band C-band/PCS, 20% mmWave.

Utilization 75% up 25% YoY, 5G traffic 68%. Low-band 70%, mid-band 88% C-band 93%, mmWave 48%.

Northeast 85%, Sunbelt 65%. DSS on 45% defers $600 million capex.

Capex $4.5 billion FY25: refarm 90 MHz, Auction 108 $2.8 billion for 80 MHz; allocate 30% FWA, 20% enterprise/media, 10% 6G.

Efficiency saves $1.3 billion opex by 2025, margins to 49%.

We are committed to sustainable network evolution.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously improving the customer experience. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value.

Enterprise and B2B at 28% of revenue, $1.52 billion up 27% YoY 9% QoQ, 11th double-digit quarter. EBITDA 42% up 450 bps, backlog $20 billion 70% in 24 months.

Pillars: 5G private networks 160 deployments up 40%, ARPU $475k/site; $300 million AutoForge, $130 million SingEco. NA 55% $880 million.

SD-WAN/SASE $560 million up 32%, 4,500 sites; $225 million GlobalBank, $100 million StreamCast. Europe 45% growth.

Edge $410 million up 52%, 2.7 million vCores; $190 million HealthNet, $120 million TechNova.

Media B2B $340 million up 22%, CDN 50 PB/day; $160 million PrimeStream, $80 million VivoPlay.

Capex $2.3 billion supports, FY $5.8 billion guide Q4 $1.65-$1.7 billion. Ahead of peers for 15-20% $100 billion market.

We are prioritizing enterprise-led customer value.

Raj Singh: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service, and develop new products and services. We are also investing in research and development to stay ahead of the curve.

Our new launches drove $720 million incremental revenue, 13% of service revenue, 2.6 million net adds up 30% QoQ.

5G Ultra FWA in 17 DMAs, $300 million revenue ARPU $88, 1.2 million adds to 4.5 million 95% YoY.

GlobalStream Plus bundles $225 million, 900k adds to 19.5 million.

Enterprise IoT $200 million ACV $120 million revenue, 500k connections.

Impact: 3.5% ARPU lift, total postpaid 120 million etc. Targeting 15-20% FY growth.

Our technological direction is converged 5G-media innovation.

Tom Harper: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making. We are also committed to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact. Our operational focus is AI-driven efficiency and green initiatives.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

David Patel: Thanks, John. Our content strategy emphasizes originals and sports co-productions to boost streaming subs and ARPU, with $500 million FY investment targeting 5 million adds and 10% ARPU lift via exclusives like expanded NFL rights, mirroring successful pivots at peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 2 million FWA subs by 2025?

Elena Vasquez: Great question, Maria. We're leveraging RDOF/BEAD subsidies and FWA on C-band for rural gaps, partnering utilities for fiber, guiding 2 million FWA via low-cost CPE and bundles, with pilots already at 1.2 million homes.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including buybacks?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, David. Priorities: 50% capex growth, 30% debt reduction to 2.3x, 20% returns—$9 billion buybacks/dividends FY25 from 45% FCF conversion, balancing investments.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

David Patel: Sarah, we're engaging FCC/EU on spectrum auctions, BEAD compliance, and DSA via lobbying, JVs for roaming, while innovating Open RAN to mitigate price caps and content mandates.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. David, would you like to provide closing remarks?

David Patel: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
